Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned counsel for the State.

This is an application under section 483 of BNSS in connection with Rourkela Sector-7 P.S. Case No.53 of 2024 corresponding to G.R. Case No.825 of 2024 pending in the Court of learned S.D.J.M.,
Panposh for the offences punishable under sections 419/420/ Designation: Senior Stenographer Reason: Authentication Location: HIGH COURT OF 451/34/120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
The petitioners moved an application for bail before the Court of learned 2nd Addl. Sessions Judge, Rourkela, which was rejected on 18.03.2025.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners are in judicial custody since 27.01.2025 and in the meantime, charge sheet has already been submitted for the offences under sections 419/420/451/34/120- B of the Indian Penal Code and taking into account the nature of accusation against the petitioners and after hearing learned counsel for the State, who submitted that the petitioner nos.1 & 2 are from the State of Bihar and petitioner no.3 is Amit Kumar Saha vs State Of Odisha .... Opp. Party on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165903076/
1 from the State of West Bengal, I am inclined to release the petitioners on bail.

sentences.text: Let the petitioners be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000.00 (rupees fifty thousand) each with two local solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the matter with further terms and conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper including the conditions that while accepting the bail bonds of the petitioners, the learned trial Court shall make address verification of the petitioners through Superintendent of Police of their respective districts and also insists for two local solvent sureties.
Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail.
The BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
